_about: Held by the Social studio on Oct 24 2026 (clarity gate: CONFUSING twice). Reversible: move an entry back to posts.json.

posts.caption:
Sunday night? Your whole week fits on one card. Five messages in, one line a day out.

Why it works: the week's deadlines hide in five different apps. Paste them in one place and the AI sorts them by day, so nothing waits in a chat you forgot to reopen.

Do this: paste the week's messages. Ask for one line a day.

The catch, from this exact run: the message said milk and dog food "before Tue". The AI put it on Tuesday. Check each line against the original message.

Made up for this post: all 5 messages. The reply is real (Claude, by Anthropic, run Oct 22, 2026), quoted exactly.

Privacy tip: delete names, addresses and account numbers before you paste.

Follow for real AI tests that give you your evenings back.

#hourback #aitips #sundayreset #weeklyplanning #familyorganization
posts.first_comment: Made-up messages, real output: Claude (Anthropic), run Oct 22, 2026 by our studio. Prompt: the 5 messages, then "Turn these into my week, Mon to Sat. One line a day: what to do, by when." The 6 lines on screen are the reply word for word. One slip ("before Tue" placed on Tue) is left in on purpose. Results vary between apps and runs.
posts.alt_text: Edited video in the Hourback look. Frame 1: big serif 'Sunday night? Your week fits on one card.' over a card titled 'Your week' with one line per day, Monday to Saturday. A rewind coin spins back to TAKE 1, in grey: five made-up message bubbles pile up. TAKE 2: the prompt is typed and the real reply card drops in. Then 'Do this: Paste the week's messages. Ask for one line a day.' with a card: 'Then check it. Ours slipped: it read "before Tue" as "on Tue."' It loops back to the opening.
